tools.tagline: Turn a large book into focused chapters.
tools.description: Split PDFs into organized chapter files using bookmarks or manual page selections. Convert EPUB and AZW3 books through Calibre before splitting.
benefits: Split by main chapters or subsections.
Use manual selections when bookmarks are unavailable.
Keep chapter files ordered with readable names.
tools.requirements: Windows 10/11; Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7+; Python 3 with pypdf. Calibre is needed for EPUB/AZW3 conversion, not ordinary PDF splitting.
tools.quick_start: Extract the complete final release, install the dependencies, then drag a supported book onto `WinBookSplit.bat`. Choose bookmark level or manual mode.
tools.output_and_limits: The current README describes chapter PDFs and a log in a new Documents folder, preserving the source. Conversion can alter layout or bookmarks; damaged/encrypted files can prevent extraction. No OCR feature is documented.
tools.editorial_note: No public release found. Current-main copy is provisional; verify dependency versions, manual-selection syntax and output behavior against final v1.0.0.

tools.description: Merge a folder of PDFs into one master document, with an optional smaller email copy. Keep source documents and existing outputs intact.
benefits: Merge top-level PDFs in natural filename order.
Create an optional email copy with Ghostscript.
Keep a local log of the merge.
tools.requirements: Windows 11 x64; Windows PowerShell 5.1 for the BAT launcher. Direct PowerShell 7.6.6 x64 invocation is documented as tested. PDFtk Server is required; Ghostscript is optional. Windows 10, ARM and live UNC shares remain unvalidated.
tools.quick_start: Extract the full package, including `src/WinPDFMerge.Helpers.ps1`. Drag exactly one source folder onto `WinPDFMerge.bat`; use PowerShell for named options.
tools.output_and_limits: Validated master PDF, optional `_email.pdf`, and log. Email output is published only when valid and smaller. Sources are not scanned recursively. Email rewriting can lose detail/features; signature validity and universal PDF feature retention are not guaranteed.
tools.editorial_note: No public release found. Verify final package and launcher acceptance before launch.

tools.tagline: Make a viewing copy. Keep the original.
tools.description: Create H.264/AAC MP4 viewing copies of videos with a focused PowerShell and FFmpeg workflow. Process individual files or folders locally.
benefits: Queue files and folders through drag and drop.
Apply a consistent CRF 22 video profile.
Preserve originals and avoid overwriting existing copies.
tools.requirements: Windows 11; Windows PowerShell 5.1 or supported stable PowerShell 7; separately supplied FFmpeg and FFprobe with required encoding capabilities. PATH takes precedence over adjacent executables.
tools.quick_start: Extract the release, supply FFmpeg/FFprobe, then open `WinVidCompress.bat` or drop videos/folders onto it. Use `-CheckEnvironment` for setup diagnostics.
tools.output_and_limits: MP4 with libx264 veryfast, CRF 22, AAC 160 kbps and faststart. Oriented height is capped at 1080 without upscale; width is not capped at 1920. Output is lossy SDR; detected HDR is refused. Extra tracks/subtitles are omitted, and output can be larger than input.
tools.editorial_note: Public v1.0.0 exists; README still gives source-ZIP/preparation wording. Website should use the release route below.

tools.description: Download podcast audio from RSS and Atom feeds to your Windows computer. Choose the latest episode, a selected count or the accessible feed catalogue.
benefits: Keep original audio without transcoding.
Verify previously downloaded files before skipping them.
Save shows for repeat or batch downloads.
tools.requirements: Windows 11; Windows PowerShell 5.1 or supported PowerShell 7; writable output storage and internet access to feed/media hosts. No FFmpeg or Python dependency.
tools.quick_start: Extract the ZIP with the complete `src` directory. Open `UniversalPodcastDownloader.bat`, enter a feed or supported show-page URL, then choose latest, count or all.
tools.output_and_limits: Audio, download history and logs in organized show folders; default root is Downloads/Podcasts. Audio includes supported MP3, M4A, Ogg, WAV and FLAC. “All” means the bounded accessible catalogue, not every historical episode. Provider feeds and discovery conventions vary; browser-session imports are unsupported.
tools.editorial_note: Public v1.0.0 exists. Software licensing does not grant rights to podcast recordings.

tools.tagline: Give spoken audio a cleaner finish.
tools.description: Clean and level speech recordings locally with PowerShell and FFmpeg. Use Raw for cleaning and leveling, or Zoom/Teams for leveling only.
benefits: Choose processing suited to the recording.
Compare short previews before full processing.
Export WAV audio with local processing reports.
tools.requirements: Windows desktop; Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7; separately supplied FFmpeg and FFprobe. Windows 10/11 are intended targets, with recorded Windows 11 checks rather than universal compatibility certification. Keep all package components together.
tools.quick_start: Extract the full tool-only ZIP, supply dependencies, and drag a simply named recording onto `WinAudioClean.bat`. Choose Raw or Zoom/Teams.
tools.output_and_limits: Default export is 48 kHz, 16-bit PCM WAV. Requested targets are −12 LUFS and −1.5 dBTP, not RMS. Accurate measurement is optional; default Fast mode does not measure final compliance. Listen to exports. Gentle is experimental and should not be promoted as an approved default.
tools.editorial_note: Public v1.0.0 exists; old internal “2.3” wording is not the public version label.

tools.tagline: Bring a mixed image folder into focus.
tools.description: Create JPEG viewing copies from mixed image folders, preserve subfolders and copy supported videos unchanged. Keep your original files untouched.
benefits: Convert supported image formats to JPEG.
Aim for a configurable file-size target.
Preserve folder structure in a fresh output tree.
tools.requirements: 64-bit Windows 10/11; Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7; ImageMagick 7.1.2-32 or a newer supported 7.x build on PATH. Windows 10 is documented but untested; decoding depends on the installed build.
tools.quick_start: Extract the package, install ImageMagick, then drag one folder onto `WinImgNormalizer.bat`. Output goes into a new Windows Pictures folder.
tools.output_and_limits: Default target is 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB), best effort. Above-target results can carry warnings. Images become sRGB JPEGs on white, with metadata removed; videos retain original bytes/metadata. Animation and multipage images produce one selected frame/page. Duplicate skipping is heuristic, not content-hash verification.
tools.editorial_note: Public v1.0.0 exists; packaged/tagged documentation retains preparation-time “unreleased” wording, acknowledged by current README.

tools.tagline: Pack more listening into your phone.
tools.description: Convert podcast and audiobook folders into compact MP3 copies with shorter filenames for phone use. Preserve the original folder structure.
benefits: Convert MP3, M4A and OGG audio in batches.
Use 64 kbps CBR by default, or choose another bitrate.
Add optional cover art and shared artist/album tags.
tools.requirements: Windows 11; Windows PowerShell or PowerShell 7; FFmpeg and FFprobe beside the script or on PATH. Exact minimum dependency versions remain to be confirmed for v1.0.0.
tools.quick_start: Extract the final release, supply dependencies, and drag a source folder onto `AudioFileForPhone.bat`.
tools.output_and_limits: New MP3 tree under Windows Music, mirrored subfolders, date-prefixed shortened filenames, collision suffixes and a run log. OGG supports Vorbis/Opus; `.opus`, WAV and FLAC are not scanned by the current documented workflow. MP3 conversion is lossy. Filename sanitizing does not establish compatibility with every phone/player. This is conversion, not the speech-cleaning workflow of WinAudioClean.
tools.editorial_note: No public release found. Current-main copy is provisional; recheck final formats, defaults and output behavior.
